name: Nutrition & Food Quality

objectives.text: Describe why the body needs a variety of foods to stay healthy and grow
Sort common farm and grocery foods into the MyPlate food groups
Identify the six classes of nutrients and name an agricultural food source for each
Compare the nutrient content of two similar food products using their Nutrition Facts labels
Explain what a calorie measures and how energy intake and physical activity together affect energy balance
Classify foods according to their nutrient density and caloric content
Identify signs of freshness and quality in fresh produce, eggs, milk, and meat
Explain how production and harvest practices such as crop variety, harvest maturity, and animal diet affect the nutritional quality of raw agricultural commodities
Explain the importance of food labeling to the consumer and interpret the required elements of a food label
Apply the Dietary Guidelines for Americans to design a balanced one-day meal plan
Compare the nutritional needs of people at different life stages, activity levels, and dietary patterns
Examine the USDA quality grades and desirable quality characteristics of products from different commodity classes such as eggs, beef, dairy, and fresh produce
Explain how changes during storage and handling such as moisture loss, oxidation, and enzymatic browning reduce the nutritional value and eating quality of foods
Evaluate nutrient content claims and health claims on food packaging against labeling regulations and nutrition facts data
Analyze nutrient analysis data from a food product to determine its nutritional value
Evaluate how a processing method such as canning, freezing, drying, or milling affects the nutritional quality of a food product
Evaluate and place food products from different commodity classes using official quality grading standards as in FFA evaluation events
Describe how consumer trends in health and nutrition influence the food products that processors develop and market
Explain how biofortified crops and nutrient-enhanced foods address micronutrient deficiencies in local and global food systems
Justify recommendations for improving the nutritional quality of a processed food formulation
Design an SAE research investigation that measures how a storage, handling, or processing variable affects the nutritional value or quality of a food product

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six existing objectives as real competencies and anchored the high school ones to matching standards. Added early objectives on food groups, nutrient classes, energy balance, freshness indicators, and how production practices shape nutritional quality. Added high school objectives on labeling and label claims, life-stage nutritional needs, USDA quality grading and FFA-style evaluation, storage-related quality loss, nutrient analysis data, consumer health trends, biofortification for global food security, and an SAE research design. Left constituent chemistry, additives, and sensory testing to the sibling sub-topics.
